open_points.subject: State 5 conventions on refusal effects across multi-step operations
open_points.text: "A refusal writes nothing" ... "When a request makes several store changes, those made before the failed one stay"
open_points.question: When an operation performs multiple store changes and later fails, is the required behavior full rollback of all earlier successful changes, or preserving earlier successful changes?
options: All-or-nothing at operation level: any failure rolls back all prior changes in that operation.
Per-store-call atomicity only: earlier successful store changes remain, later failing change is absent.
Per refusal code behavior: some refusals roll back all, others keep earlier changes.
open_points.default_guess: Per-store-call atomicity only (earlier successful changes remain), because later text states this explicitly for failed later store changes.

open_points.subject: public_op:store.spool_file attempt-level cleanup semantics
open_points.text: "Inputs ... the file's bytes" ... "`refused` over a spool ceiling, nothing kept of that file or of any file that attempt spooled before (A15 rule 3)"
open_points.question: How is "nothing kept ... of any file that attempt spooled before" enforced when spooling is called per-file?
options: `store.spool_file` must purge all files already spooled for that attempt on ceiling refusal.
Caller must issue compensating deletions for earlier files of the same attempt.
Spooling for one attempt must be batched into a single call so refusal is naturally atomic.
open_points.default_guess: `store.spool_file` purges previously spooled files for that attempt on refusal.

open_points.subject: effects.recover_in_flight_attempts processing order
open_points.text: "At start, turn every in_flight attempt unknown with its record."
open_points.question: In what deterministic order are multiple `in_flight` attempts recovered and written?
options: Newest first in reverse store order.

open_points.subject: get_repair_view continuation when slot implementation set changes
open_points.text: "passed back, it pages only the NodeExecutions, and every other part is read again as of that request"
open_points.question: For `get_repair_view` pagination, is the NodeExecution filter set (slot implementations) frozen from page 1 or recomputed on each continuation request?
options: Freeze the implementation-id filter set in the continuation token for stable paging.
Recompute the implementation-id filter each request; token validity depends on the new filter and may become invalid.
Recompute filter and ignore mismatch, allowing shifted/partial pagination.
open_points.default_guess: Recompute each request, and token becomes invalid if filter canonical form changed.
